headline: The characters were being drawn inside-out. Three separate geometry generators had inverted triangle winding; the two that build the whole body meant 153,344 of 227,850 triangles rendered with their normal facing away from the camera, so WebGL culled the near surface and drew the inside of the far one. That is the see-through report, it is not a hole, and no amount of hole-filling could ever have reached it.
evidence_scope: The winding claim is a RASTERISATION claim, not an appearance claim, and that distinction is why software frames are admissible for it: back-face culling by screen-space winding is core GL behaviour, identical under SwiftShader and hardware. The signed-volume numbers are geometry, computed offline from vertex buffers, with no renderer involved at all. Everything about how the new face, girdle and proportions LOOK under light is an appearance claim and I have not made one.

done_and_measured.instrument: tools/visual/mesh-winding.mjs (new). Signed volume + authored-normal agreement + boundary-edge closure, per mesh and per generator.
done_and_measured.before: 65 of 715 meshes NEGATIVE signed volume. 153,344 of 227,850 triangles (67.3%) whose authored normal disagrees with their winding. actor-body:<family>:skin 13/13 inverted (102,708/109,792). actor-body:<family>:cloth 13/13 inverted (49,088/51,896).

three_generators_and_each_was_wrong_diff: MeshBuilder.tube/.ball/.ellipsoid — side walls wound A,C,B, giving a face normal of -_u (inward). tube's END CAPS were always correct, which is why the disagreement was 94% and not 100%: one mesh carried both conventions.

garmentTabGeometry — the entire index list inverted. INVISIBLE to a normal-agreement check, because computeVertexNormals() derives normals FROM the winding, so the normals agreed with a wrong surface. Only signed volume caught it (13/13 `:legs` meshes negative). This is why the instrument measures both and not one.
torsoShellGeometry — CAPS ONLY, walls always correct. 36 triangles per shell, matching the measured 144/720 on `tailored-tunic` over 4 meshes exactly.

All seven THREE built-ins used by the presentation path measure positive. The comparison is against the engine's own geometry, not against my reasoning about GL.

done_and_measured.id: C. verdict §7 fix 2 — the canon of proportion
done_and_measured.before: 41 shipped figures, R = height/head: min 5.87, median 6.58, max 6.84. 0 of 41 in band. 6 of 41 outside the hard band.
done_and_measured.after: min 7.43, median 7.59, max 7.90. 41 of 41 in band (100%). 0 outside the hard band. ACCEPTANCE MET.
done_and_measured.how: A flat 0.80 head scale got the median to 7.43 but left 7 of 41 outside, and the residual TRACKED `build` — because head extent is the skull above the head bone PLUS the neck joint ball below it, and that ball's radius derives from the neck tube's r1 and so scales with build. Solved rather than hand-tuned: hs = (TARGET_EXTENT - 0.070*build) / headTopLocal, with the crest entering headTopLocal only when it actually rises above the crown. Spread collapsed from 0.97 wide to 0.47 wide. Bone offsets are untouched — they are where the hurtboxes live.
done_and_measured.design_rule_encoded: build and crest are ornament axes. A character may be heavier, leaner or more crested than another; it may not thereby be a different number of heads tall.
